title: development CI commitlint hatasını yeniden üret ve gider
name: ci-commit-messages
description: GitHub Actions lint işindeki commit messages adımının development PR’larında neden kırmızı olduğunu gerçek commit aralığı ve commitlint yapılandırması üzerinden teşhis et. .github/workflows/ci.yml ve commitlint.config.js için gereken en dar düzeltmeyi yap; PR ve push koşullarını doğrula. Bir node değişikliğine changeset ekleme veya release bump seçme.

brief.approach:
**Diagnosis (already reproduced; do not re-derive, verify only).**

The `commit messages` step in the `lint` job (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:29-31`) runs `commitlint --from origin/<base_ref> --to HEAD` on every pull request. It went red on five development PRs on 2026-09-23 (runs 35918937479, 35922717194, 35923553879, 35925034827, 35927325176 — session-mock, transcript-adr, tool-colour, text-lines, line-detail). In each, the node's own commits passed; the failures were older commits that were in the node branch but not yet on `origin/development`, because SOBER cuts a node's branch from **local** `development`, which carried unpushed merges. Once `development` was pushed those commits left the range and development PRs went green again (every run since is green on this step).

The defect has not gone away; it has moved. Those commits are now on `origin/development`, so they sit in `origin/main..origin/development`, the range the next release PR into `main` will lint. Today `pnpm exec commitlint --from origin/main --to origin/development` fails on exactly seven commits:

- `2d8ac64` `design: replace graph pulse with EKG trace, add motion-force switch`, type-enum
- `17495e4` `design: refine watch-the-run graph pulse and session motion`, type-enum
- `7a27b3b` `fix(core): prefer Git's bin/sh.exe, which puts /usr/bin on PATH`, body-max-line-length
- `17c2de0` `fix(core): start npm-installed hosts on Windows through their script`, body-max-line-length
- `67473e3` `fix(core): run sober's own entry for openrouter on Windows`, body-max-line-length
- `5d6f986` `feat(core): dispatch refusals name the config key to edit`, body-max-line-length
- `c1597e8` `fix: advance the test board with a commit git will not deduplicate`, body-max-line-length

`development` is shared and pushed, so rewriting those commits is off the table.

**Change: `commitlint.config.js` only.**

Add an `ignores` entry that skips exactly those seven landed commits, matched on the **exact first line** of the message: a `Set` of the seven subjects and `ignores: [(message) => LANDED.has(message.split('\n')[0].trim())]`. Add a comment in the file's existing style (like the `subject-case` and `sober` comments) saying these are already on `development`, cannot be rewritten, and are listed so the release range can pass; new commits are not covered. Keep `defaultIgnores` on (the merge-commit ignore is needed for the PR merge ref). Change no rule: `design` stays a scope (`docs(design):`, `fix(design):` are the convention), and `body-max-line-length` stays at 100.

**`.github/workflows/ci.yml`: no change. Record the check in the commit body.** The step's condition `github.event_name == 'pull_request'` is correct. `push` only fires for `main`, where a merge is a release already linted as its PR, and development PRs use `base_ref`. The `--from origin/<base_ref>` range is right; what made it noisy was branches cut from an unpushed local base, which is a dispatch concern and out of scope here.

**Commit message:** conventional, body lines ≤100 chars, e.g. `ci: let commitlint pass the seven commits already on development`. No changeset (CLAUDE.md). Do not touch `package.json`.

acceptance.proves: The range the next release PR into main will lint passes. Before this change it failed on the seven landed commits.

acceptance.run:
node -e "const {spawnSync}=require('child_process');const lint=m=>spawnSync('pnpm exec commitlint',{input:m,shell:true}).status;const cases=[['design: a new design-typed commit',1],['fix(core): a new commit

'+'x'.repeat(101),1],['design: refine watch-the-run graph pulse and session motion',0],['fix(core): start npm-installed hosts on Windows through their script

'+'x'.repeat(150),0],['feat(core): an ordinary new commit',0]];let bad=0;for(const [m,want] of cases){const got=lint(m)===0?0:1;if(got!==want){bad++;console.error((want?'should fail, passed: ':'should pass, failed: ')+m.split('
')[0])}}if(bad)process.exit(1);console.log('ok')"
acceptance.proves: The exemption is narrow. A new `design:` commit and a new commit with a 101-character body line still fail. Only the listed historical subjects pass, and an ordinary commit still passes.
The node's own commits pass the same check the development PR will run.
The workflow, package.json and changesets are untouched. The fix is the config alone, with no changeset.
The formatter and secret scan still pass with the edited config file.
